academic_translation:
If, without a sprout, a tree never emerges in the world,
How could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits emerge on it?
If, without the mind of awakening, a Victor does not emerge in the world,
How could the fruits—Śakra, Brahmā, and śrāvakas—emerge?
translation: If there is no sprout, a tree could never grow in the world. Without a tree, how could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit ever appear? In the same way, without the wish to awaken, a Victorious One would never appear in the world. Without a Victorious One, how could the fruits—like Shakra, Brahma, and listeners—ever appear?

academic_translation:
This Dharma of the Guides is profound and difficult to see;
It is not realized by anyone, nor is there any attaining of it.
Therefore, the Compassionate Benefactor, having attained awakening,
Felt little inclination, thinking, "Who among the masses of sentient beings will understand?"
translation: This teaching of the Guides is deep and hard to see. No one has realized it, and there is nothing to be reached. So, when the Kind Helper reached awakening, he paused. He thought, "Who among all the living beings will understand this?"

academic_translation:
When training, whoever does not assert any training at all,
Does not apprehend a trainee or the phenomena of training,
And does not conceptualize these two—training and non-training—
Whoever trains like that trains here in the qualities of a Buddha.
translation: When doing their training, they do not cling to the training itself. They do not grasp at a learner or at the things to train in. They do not hold on to the ideas of training or not training. Anyone who practices like this is training in a Buddha's qualities.
